name: gravity
why: An embeddable programming language, obscure enough to be a fun side trip into language design.

brief.what_it_is: Gravity is a dynamically typed, lightweight, embeddable programming language written in C with no external dependencies beyond the C standard library. It is class-based with Swift-like syntax, and supports procedural, object-oriented, functional, and data-driven styles, plus prototype-style use via special built-in methods. The CLI takes a .gravity source file (or inline code with -i) and runs it, or compiles it to bytecode with -c. The project also ships a library (libgravity) that host applications can embed.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says Gravity was developed from scratch for the Creo project to offer an easy way to write portable code for iOS and Android. It is written in portable C99 so it can be compiled on any platform.
brief.how_it_works: A multipass compiler with an optimizer turns source into bytecode, which runs on a stack-based VM. The source tree is split into compiler/ (lexer, parser, AST, semantic analysis, IR, optimizer, codegen), runtime/ (stack VM and built-in types), and shared/ (value representation, hash table, array, mark-and-sweep GC). Coroutines are implemented as fibers.

commands_seen.context: Builds the gravity CLI executable on Linux, macOS, and BSD.

Runs the unit test suite through the VM.

brief.install_notes: Building from source is the documented route in the README. Make works on Linux, macOS, and BSD. CMake covers Windows and needs a C99 compiler; there are no external dependencies. The README does not mention Homebrew-specific steps. A fuller getting-started guide is linked from the docs site.
brief.standout: It is a full language (classes, closures, GC, fibers, JSON, optional modules) in roughly 20K lines of C, and the README says the compiler and VM add under 200KB to a 64-bit executable. Its syntax is Swift-like and it treats optional semicolons as a feature. Its closures design credits the Lua closures paper, and its fibers and GC draw on Wren.

The GitHub README is detailed and current-looking (it lists CMake, a changelog, and an architecture doc), but it shows no release date or last-commit info, so I cannot confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: The homepage fetch returned almost no content, so the description comes from the GitHub README. The README names Creo and the Untold game engine as the main known users. Only a C99 compiler is needed, but the embedding API is C-only in what I read, and the bridging documentation lives on the external docs site. The homepage was thin, so the full language documentation was not verified.
quotes: Gravity is a powerful, dynamically typed, lightweight, embeddable programming language written in C without any external dependencies (except for stdlib).
It is a class-based concurrent scripting language with modern Swift-like syntax.
The compiler and virtual machine combined add less than 200KB to the executable on a 64-bit system.
Gravity is available under the permissive MIT license.
